title: BCD Converter
description: Convert decimal numbers to Binary-Coded Decimal (packed and unpacked) and decode BCD back to decimal, with per-digit nibble breakdowns.
howto: Choose decimal → BCD or BCD → decimal.
For decimal → BCD pick packed (two digits per byte) or unpacked (one nibble per digit) display.
Press Convert to see each digit as a 4-bit nibble plus the byte/hex view.
For BCD → decimal, paste nibbles like 1001 0011 and get the decoded number.

faqs.a: Binary-Coded Decimal encodes each decimal digit in its own 4-bit nibble (0→0000 … 9→1001). Packed BCD stores two digits per byte; unpacked BCD uses one byte per digit.

faqs.q: Why use BCD instead of binary?
faqs.a: BCD avoids binary↔decimal rounding surprises, so it is used in financial systems, digital clocks and seven-segment display drivers where exact decimal digits matter.

faqs.q: Which nibbles are invalid in BCD?
faqs.a: 1010 through 1111 (A–F) are not valid BCD digits. The decoder rejects them and tells you exactly which nibble is bad.
